title: Eligibility-traces laboratory
summary: TD(λ) step by step with every state's trace; the three kinds of trace (Figure 7.9) and the half-life of λ; the 19-state random-walk experiments of Figures 7.2 and 7.6 for n-step, λ-return, TD(λ) with each trace and true on-line TD(λ); and the credit one episode gives with and without traces (Example 7.2), including Watkins's cut.
guide: Step TD(λ) with λ = 0.8: nothing changes until the first reward; then every state visited in that episode moves, the most recent most.
Set λ = 0 and step: only the state just left changes. That is TD(0).

In the trace panel, compare the three traces after the four quick visits: accumulating climbs above 2, replacing stays at 1, dutch lies between. Set α (dutch) to 0 or 1 to see it become the other two.

Run the on-line n-step family: the best curves are intermediate n near α = 0.4–0.5 (about 0.27). Then the off-line family: errors are higher and everything blows up above α ≈ 0.3; n = 3 and n = 5 break down earliest (Exercise 7.3).
Run accumulating, dutch and true on-line TD(λ): accumulating blows up for λ ≥ 0.95 at large α, the other two stay stable.
In 'Credit from one episode', compare the two grids, then declare a move exploratory to see Watkins's Q(λ) give nothing to the moves before it.
